title: Reporting Capital Gains on MFs: A Guide for AY26-27
description: Accurately reporting capital gains from mutual fund investments in your Income Tax Return is mandatory. Equity-oriented and debt-oriented mutual funds are sub.

faq.q: What is the difference between equity and debt MFs for tax purposes?
faq.a: Equity MFs (65%+ equity) have specific LTCG (10% over ₹1L) and STCG (15%) rates. Debt MFs (less than 65% equity) sold in FY25-26 have all gains added to your income and taxed at your slab rate.

faq.q: Do I need to report losses from MFs?
faq.a: Yes, it is mandatory to report capital losses. While you don't pay tax on losses, reporting them allows you to carry forward these losses to offset future capital gains for up to 8 assessment years.

faq.q: What is the grandfathering rule for equity MFs?
faq.a: The grandfathering rule applies to equity mutual fund units purchased before January 31, 2018. For LTCG calculation, the cost of acquisition is considered the higher of the actual purchase price or the NAV as of January 31, 2018, protecting gains accrued before this date.

faq.q: How are debt MFs taxed after April 1, 2023?
faq.a: For all debt mutual fund units sold in FY25-26 (AY26-27), the gains are added to your total income and taxed as per your applicable income tax slab rate. The indexation benefit and the distinction between STCG/LTCG are no longer applicable.

faq.q: Can I adjust capital losses against gains?
faq.a: Yes, short-term capital losses can be set off against both short-term and long-term capital gains. Long-term capital losses can only be set off against long-term capital gains. Unadjusted losses can be carried forward for 8 years.

faq.q: What is a Consolidated Account Statement (CAS)?
faq.a: A CAS is a single statement provided by RTAs (like CAMS or KFintech) that summarises all your mutual fund transactions across different fund houses, making it easier to track your investments and calculate gains.

faq.q: Which ITR form should I use for capital gains?
faq.a: Most salaried individuals with capital gains from mutual funds will use ITR-2. If you also have income from "Profits and Gains from Business or Profession," you would typically use ITR-3.
